title: Weighted ball scaling for conical measures
statement_lean:
theorem integral_homogeneous_closedBall
    (μ : Measure (Euclidean n)) (hcone : IsConical m μ)
    (h : Euclidean n → ℝ) (hh : Measurable h) (a : ℝ)
    (hhom : ∀ r > 0, ∀ z, h (r • z) = r ^ a * h z)
    (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) :
    (∫ z in closedBall 0 r, h z ∂μ) =
      r ^ ((m : ℝ) + a) * ∫ z in closedBall 0 1, h z ∂μ
statement_tex: For a conical measure $\mu$ and a measurable real-valued function $h$ homogeneous of arbitrary real degree $a$, for every $r>0$, $\int_{\overline B(0,r)}h\,d\mu=r^{m+a}\int_{\overline B(0,1)}h\,d\mu$. No positivity or integrability assumption is needed for this scaling identity; both sides use the Bochner nonintegrable-value convention.
status: Local Lean/kernel check passed with only standard axioms; canonical integration CI pending.
source: Direct change of variables in the conical scaling identity; reusable supporting lemma for De Lellis homogeneous radial integration.
